text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat due in Amman today after bad weather delayed yesterday's scheduled visit.

- Authorities prepare five million dinar ($7.1 million) tender to be issued in March for infrastructure on eastern coast of the Dead Sea. Includes supplying electricity and maintenance of water pipes.

- In his only contact with another Arab leader, Sudan's military leader President Bashir called King Hussein to thank him for his solid support for Sudan and to reassure him about the situation on Sudan's eastern borders.

- United Nations sources say will start paying Gulf War compensation in two weeks' time to claimants seeking damages of up to $100,000. There are 65,000 requests from 81 countries worth a total of $476 million.
- "If it weren't for King Hussein's efforts, we wouldn't be in Hebron today," Arafat tells Ad-Dustour.
- Ministry of planning sources say the International Monetary Fund is very happy with Jordan's economic reform and Jordan is likely to get up to $360 million in loans from the fund up to 1998.
- King Hussein affirms he underwent two knee surgeries, thanks Jordanians for their concern.
